To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have obtained NNLO threshold corrections to the production of W and Z gauge bosons at the LHC, and that the corrections are moderate and significantly reduce the scale uncertainty.
the next-to-next- to-leading order corrections to the threshold cross section of electroweek bosons are moderate and reduce the scale uncertainties significantly.
the next-to-nextto-leading order corrections to the transverse-momentum spectrum of a W, Z or Higgs boson near the threshold are large and reduce the scale dependence of the spectrum.

the production of W, Z, and Higgs boson in the threshold limit in the Standard Model and beyond.
the production of electroweek bosons near the threshold of partonic collisions.
the calculation of the next-to-nextto-leading-order corrections to transverse momentum spectra of electrowek bosons near the threshold.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two-loop corrections are large but not overwhelming.
the NLO corrections are large enough to warrant an NLO calculation and that the NNLO corrections are small enough to warrant the use of the NNLO calculation.
the NNLO corrections are moderate and that the theoretical uncertainties are reduced significantly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NNLO corrections for the electroweaks bosons are under good control, and that they can be used to obtain reliable predictions for the cross sections in the threshold limit.

The main takeaway from our work is that
threshold resummation is an essential ingredient for precise theoretical predictions for W, Z and h production at hadron colliders.
the threshold resummation of transverse-momentum distributions for W and Z boson production is under control at next-to-next to leading order and can be reliably used in the analysis of LHC data.
